verdicts.tldr: a failed base render is never reported as a new realm; the note comes from the merge-base tree alone
verdicts.details: renderBase returns (nil, newRealms) on every failure path (main.go:256, 270, 274, 278), and ScreenshotPairs reads New from that map alone. shots.go:85-88 says so in as many words: "New in this PR is asserted only from the merge-base tree, never inferred from a missing capture: a base pass that ran but failed on this realm would otherwise be reported as the realm not existing." So a realm whose before shot crashed keeps New=false and no note, while a realm absent at the merge base keeps its note, and the two read differently in the comment. Only the -base-root-absent path returns a nil map, and there no realm gets a before column at all, which is the only thing a run with no merge base can honestly say. Fix: none needed; if the no-base run is worth marking, say it once above the grid rather than per pair.
verdicts.evidence: read of shots.go:66-92 and main.go:231-279. shots.go:77 pair := ShotPair{Realm: r, URL: path.Dir(afterFile) + "/", New: newRealms[r]}; shots.go:88 if base != nil { — every renderBase error path above it still returns newRealms.
verdicts.refuted_by: shots.go:85-87 // "New in this PR" is asserted only from the merge-base tree, never // inferred from a missing capture: a base pass that ran but failed on // this realm would otherwise be reported as the realm not existing.
verdicts.verify_by: run render without -base-root on a plan with a changed realm and read comment.md: the pair block has no <sub>New in this PR</sub> line | run render with -base-root pointing at a checkout where the base gnodev cannot start (or chrome absent), and diff the produced comment.md against the same run with a working base: the before column vanishes with no note

verdicts.tldr: -port 0 is accepted and costs the full 5-minute timeout before reporting a message that names no port
verdicts.details: Nothing between fs.Parse and use range-checks cfg.port (main.go:69 declares it, main.go in full carries no validation). With -port 0 gnodev is told -web-listener 127.0.0.1:0, binds a random port and stays alive, while main.go:124 builds Base as http://127.0.0.1:0 and waitReady dials that. The died channel only carries a value when gnodev exits (main.go:199-204), so the select at crawl.go:597-601 never takes it and the loop sleeps a second at a time to the deadline. The operator waits the full -timeout and gets "gnoweb not ready after 5m0s", which names neither the flag nor the port it produced. Fix: listen on :0 in-process, read the bound port back, and reject 0 at flag time.
verdicts.evidence: read of main.go:69 (flag, no check), main.go:124 (Base built straight from cfg.port), main.go:199-204 (died fires only on cmd.Wait) and crawl.go:589-610 (waitReady loops to the deadline, returning "gnoweb not ready after %s"). Triggering input: gnopreview render -port 0.
verdicts.verify_by: gnopreview render -port 0 on any plan: expect a clear error, observe a 5 minute wait then "gnoweb not ready"

verdicts.tldr: a mistyped subcommand blocks on stdin and walks every examples package before saying the command does not exist
verdicts.details: run() calls readLines at main.go:87 and BuildPlan at main.go:91, and only then reaches the switch at :96 that decides whether the command exists. -changed defaults to "-" (main.go:66) and readLines("-") reads /dev/stdin (main.go:309-310), so `gnopreview redner` from a terminal hangs with no output; fed an EOF it walks examples/gno.land through LoadPkgs before printing unknown command "redner". The user loses a typo's worth of time to a hang whose cause the program already knows. Fix: switch on cmd immediately after fs.Parse and let each command do its own reading.
verdicts.evidence: read of main.go:56-103 and main.go:306-324. The ordering is literal: changed, err := readLines(cfg.changed) at :87, plan, err := BuildPlan(...) at :91, switch cmd at :96, return fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q", cmd) at :102.
verdicts.verify_by: go run . redner in misc/gnopreview with stdin a terminal: expect the usage error, observe the process blocked on the stdin read

verdicts.tldr: -port above 55535 derives an out-of-range RPC port and fails naming a number the operator never typed
verdicts.details: startGnodev builds the node listener as tcp://127.0.0.1:%d with port+10000 (main.go:176) and nothing validates cfg.port (main.go:69). -port 56000 asks gnodev to bind 66000, outside the u16 range, so the process exits, died fires and waitReady returns "gnodev exited before serving" (crawl.go:598-599) pointing at a log about port 66000. The base pass at cfg.port+1 (main.go:251) fails the same way. The cost is a confusing failure on a flag the tool could have rejected. Fix: bound cfg.port to 1..55534 right after fs.Parse and name both derived ports in the error.
verdicts.evidence: read of main.go:167-179 and main.go:56-95. Line 176: "-node-rpc-listener", fmt.Sprintf("tcp://127.0.0.1:%d", port+10000) — 56000+10000 = 66000 > 65535, and no check stands between fs.Parse at :77 and the call at :117.
verdicts.verify_by: gnopreview render -port 56000 with a built gnodev: expect a flag error, observe a bind failure on 66000

verdicts.tldr: the listing branch of urlToFile is dead in the binary, so a test row promises snapshots of gnoweb listings that are never taken
verdicts.details: No URL the crawler captures can end in a slash. Seeds builds every entry from urlOf and path.Dir (crawl.go:85-99) and its directory walk stops while strings.Count(d, "/") >= 2, so it never emits "/" or a trailing slash; inScope returns false for any base ending in "/" (crawl.go:191-193), and Run only enqueues a link that is a seed or in scope. So urlToFile's listing branch never fires outside its own test, and TestURLToFile's {"/r/", "r/_dir/index.html"} row is the only thing that exercises it. A reader who trusts that row will assume gnoweb's directory listings are in the snapshot; they are left to the live site. Fix: drop the branch and its row, and say in the Seeds comment that listings go to the live site.
verdicts.evidence: read of crawl.go:73-105 (Seeds), 105-150 (Run's queue admission), 186-196 (inScope's trailing-slash reject) and 487-494 (the listing flag). crawl.go:191-193: // "/r/x/y/" is gnoweb's listing view ... if strings.HasSuffix(base, "/") { return false }. crawl_test.go:83 pins {"/r/gnoland/home/", false}.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestListingBranchNeverRuns: a fake gnoweb linking "/r/x/y/" on every page, then assert no captured URL ends in "/" and no File contains "/_dir/" | cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestProbeListingBranchUnreachable -v . with the probe file: seeds carry no trailing slash and inScope is false for every trailing-slash form

verdicts.tldr: the test states an invariant about unsafe path characters that it never asserts and urlToFile never enforces on the base segment
verdicts.details: The header at crawl_test.go:51-52 reads "No output path may contain $, : or & — they survive a URL but not every static host", and the table under it compares seven exact strings, none of which carries one of those characters in the base. urlToFile slugs args and query and passes base through untouched (crawl.go:487-493), so urlToFile("/r/x&y") returns "r/x&y/index.html". Nothing reaches it today because inScope requires base to equal a selected realm's path, so what is lost is a documented invariant no test holds, not a live bug. Fix: assert it over the table — strings.ContainsAny(got, "$:&") must be false for every row — instead of stating it in prose.
verdicts.evidence: read of crawl_test.go:49-68 and crawl.go:480-494. splitURL cuts on "$" and ":" only (crawl.go:276-280), so "&" stays in base; base = strings.Trim(base, "/") is appended to parts with no slug() call, while args and query both go through slug().
verdicts.verify_by: add {"/r/x&y", ...} to TestURLToFile's table and grep the output for "&"; the existing assertions never look at the characters

verdicts.tldr: cleanup and publish share a concurrency group only while the fork still exists, and a deleted fork is a common way a PR closes
verdicts.details: The two groups are built from different event payloads: cleanup keys on github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name and head.ref (pr-preview-cleanup.yml:22-24), publish on github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name and head_branch (pr-preview-publish.yml:32-35). They agree while the fork exists. GitHub leaves pull_request.head.repo null once the fork is deleted — which itself auto-closes the PR — and the group then renders as pr-preview-publish--<ref>, not the publish's group, so the close no longer serializes behind an in-flight publish and that publish's replay loop can re-add pr-<N>/ after the cleanup removed it. The preview then survives the closed PR until the previews repo's own daily sweep. Fix: key both workflows on the pull request number, which is never null on either payload.
verdicts.evidence: read of both concurrency blocks, quoted above. Attempted to exhibit the null: gh api 'repos/gnolang/gno/pulls?state=closed&per_page=100' --jq '[.[]|select(.head.repo==null)|{n:.number}]' returned [] over the latest 100 closed PRs, so the null-payload case is not reproducible in this environment. Confirming it needs a closed PR whose fork was deleted, or a workflow_run/pull_request_target payload pair captured from a real close.
verdicts.verify_by: gh api repos/gnolang/gno/pulls/<a closed PR whose fork was deleted> --jq '.head.repo' returns null; compare the two concurrency expressions at pr-preview-cleanup.yml:22 and pr-preview-publish.yml:34

verdicts.tldr: the preview homepage claims more realms rendered than it lists, and names none of the ones missing
verdicts.details: Index builds its rows from p.Realms and skips every realm absent from c.pages (comment.go:168-171), then prints the count as len(p.Realms) (comment.go:191 and :195). A realm gnoweb answered non-200 for, or one getRetry failed on, is counted and not listed: Run logs "! %s: HTTP %d" and continues (crawl.go:126-133) without recording the page. The reviewer reads "25 realm(s) rendered" over 23 links with nothing saying which two are gone. Fix: count the rows as they are written, and list the skipped realms as a short "not rendered" line.
verdicts.evidence: read of comment.go:166-196 and crawl.go:118-140. comment.go:170 if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok { continue }; comment.go:195 ..., len(p.Realms), rows.String()).
verdicts.verify_by: crawl with a stub gnodev returning 500 for one seed realm, then read the generated index.html: the count exceeds the number of <li> rows | cp the artifact and run `go test ./... -run TestB5IndexCountMatchesItsList -v` in misc/gnopreview | cp tests/b5-refactor-index-parity_test.go misc/gnopreview/ && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestUnrenderedRealmParity -v ./...

verdicts.tldr: the _dir branch cannot run, and four test rows pin a trailing-slash shape the crawler never produces
verdicts.details: The listing flag is strings.HasSuffix(base, "/") && base != "/" (crawl.go:490), and no crawled URL ends in a slash: Seeds builds from urlOf and path.Dir (crawl.go:85-99) and inScope rejects any trailing-slash base (crawl.go:191-193), so Run's queue never holds one. TestSplitURL's {"/r/x/y/", ...} row, TestCanonicalURL's {"/r/x/y/", "/r/x/y/"} row and TestURLToFile's {"/r/", "r/_dir/index.html"} row therefore guard a shape the binary cannot reach. They read as coverage of the directory-listing path while the real listing link is the one silently going offsite. Fix: delete the branch and those rows, keeping TestCrawlerInScope's {"/r/gnoland/home/", false} as the statement that listings are left to the live site.
verdicts.evidence: read of crawl.go:485-505, 73-105 and 186-196, with crawl_test.go:16, 36, 63 and 83 as the pinned rows. The finder's named tests TestURLToFileIsSafe and TestSplitURLKeepsTrailingSlash do not exist under those names in crawl_test.go; the rows above are what pin the shape.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestReachDirListingBranchIsDead -v . : assert inScope("/r/gnoland/") is false and that no Seeds() entry ends in "/"

verdicts.tldr: the marker and heading are built and then thrown away, and the guard that throws them away has no caller
verdicts.details: Comment writes CommentMarker and the heading into b at comment.go:19-20, then returns "" at :24 when p.Empty(), discarding both. The guard has no live caller: render() returns at main.go:111-114 before it ever reaches Comment at main.go:156, so the only thing exercising :24 is plan_test.go:181. A reader adding a branch after :20 has to notice the discarded prefix first, which is the cost. Fix: move the p.Empty() check above the two WriteString calls, three lines up.
verdicts.evidence: read of comment.go:17-26 and main.go:105-158, plus grep for Comment( across the package: main.go:156 and plan_test.go:181, 194, 222, 244, 271 are every call site, and main.go:111 if plan.Empty() { ... return writeJSON(...) } stands above the only non-test one.
verdicts.verify_by: read main.go:105-158 for the early return at :111, then comment.go:17-26 | move the p.Empty() guard above the builder in comment.go, then cd misc/gnopreview && gofmt -l . && go test ./...

verdicts.tldr: in gnoweb mode the realm list drops the source and help links, in the very mode where source and help rendering is what changed
verdicts.details: comment.go:44 writes link(urlOf(r), r) alone, while both default-branch lists write link(...) + tabs(base, r) at :63 and :80. The pages are in the snapshot: Seeds adds u+"$source" and u+"$help" for every realm whenever RenderOnly is false (crawl.go:85-92), and the gnoweb-mode crawler is built with RenderOnly unset (main.go:123-130). The reviewer has to hand-edit URLs to reach the two tabs the change is about. Fix: append tabs(base, r) at :44, matching :63 and :80.
verdicts.evidence: read of comment.go:36-54 against :60-82 and :148-155, and crawl.go:85-99. comment.go:44 b.WriteString("- " + link(urlOf(r), r) + "\n") vs comment.go:63 b.WriteString("- " + link(urlOf(r), r) + tabs(base, r) + "\n").
verdicts.verify_by: read comment.go:43-45 against :63 and :80, and crawl.go:85-93 for the $source/$help seeds

verdicts.tldr: the comment tells the reviewer realm sources changed when only a p/ package did
verdicts.details: Mode() returns "both" whenever p.Gnoweb is set and either ChangedRealms or ChangedPkgs is non-empty (plan.go:95-97), so a PR touching gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ and one examples p/ package lands in the default branch with ChangedRealms empty. comment.go:48 then opens "This PR changes **gnoweb** and realm sources." while the body below prints no Changed realms section at all (comment.go:60 gates it on len(p.ChangedRealms) > 0), only the indirect list. The reviewer is told to look for realm source changes that are not in the diff. Fix: gate the sentence on len(p.ChangedRealms) > 0 and word the package-only case as gnoweb plus a changed package.
verdicts.evidence: read of plan.go:92-104 (Mode) and comment.go:36-82. plan.go: case p.Gnoweb && len(p.ChangedRealms) == 0 && len(p.ChangedPkgs) == 0: return "gnoweb" / case p.Gnoweb: return "both" — ChangedPkgs alone is enough to reach "both".
verdicts.verify_by: the TestReachB5CommentHidesIndirectSeedRealm output above: ChangedRealms is empty and the sentence is in the body
